headline: Red Sox land NLCS MVP Jake Bauers for four years

off.text: Next: Sun, Nov 15 at Lions (Munich), 9:30 AM
Next: Sun, Nov 15 vs Mavericks, 6:00 PM

storylines: Boston (13–5–1) is third in the Atlantic after Thursday's 5–2 loss to Montreal, which ended a four-game winning streak.
Minnesota leads the Central with 32 points and beat Boston 4–1 on Oct. 3 in Minnesota.
Marco Sturm shuffled two defense pairs at Friday's practice and will settle them Saturday; James Hagens (back) is still on injured reserve.
bruins.edge: Minnesota: five more points with two more games played, and only three regulation losses to Boston's five.

storylines: New England (5–4) faces Detroit (6–2) in Munich after allowing 45 points to Green Bay, its most in a regular-season game since 1993.
A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are among nine Patriots listed as questionable; TreVeyon Henderson, Carlton Davis and Ben Brown are out.
Mike Vrabel said he felt "pretty good" about Brown and Stevenson after watching them practice in Germany.
patriots.edge: Detroit: a better record, and New England has three players out and nine more questionable.

storylines: Boston comes home on a five-game winning streak after a 4–0 road trip, and hasn't played since Wednesday.
Jayson Tatum is third on the NBA's MVP ladder, averaging 26.3 points, 7.5 assists and 6.1 rebounds.
Sam Hauser is plus-125 in 252 minutes, eighth in the league, and is shooting 43.5 percent from three.
celtics.edge: Boston: the East's best record at 10–2 and at home, against a 7–5 Dallas team.

bruins.headline: Pairings shuffled after a video day
bruins.summary: Friday's practice was mostly video of the Montreal loss. Marco Sturm paired Frederic Brunet with Connor Clifton and Mason Lohrei with Jonathan Aspirot, but said he'd decide Saturday; the forward lines stayed the same. James Hagens (IR) watched part of practice, and Sturm said he's "doing really good."

bruins.headline: Swayman pulled for the first time this season
bruins.summary: Jeremy Swayman was pulled after allowing four goals on 17 shots in 28:14 against Montreal, Boston's first in-game goalie change this season. Swayman said he trusted Marco Sturm's decision, and David Pastrnak said, "It's on us."

bruins.headline: Sturm: 'We were just very flat'
bruins.summary: Marco Sturm said Boston's effort was lacking in Thursday's 5–2 loss, which ended a seven-game home winning streak and moved Montreal ahead of the Bruins in the Atlantic. Boston hosts Minnesota on Saturday.

bruins.headline: Bergeron inducted; number retired Dec. 1
bruins.summary: Patrice Bergeron was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in Toronto as one of six members of the Class of 2026. The Bruins retire his number at TD Garden on Dec. 1, with the ceremony starting at 6:10 p.m.

bruins.headline: Hagens out a few weeks after a crosscheck
bruins.summary: James Hagens went on injured reserve after a crosscheck to the back on Thursday and is expected to miss a few weeks. Mikey Eyssimont, recalled from Providence, scored in his season debut against Florida.

bruins.headline: McAvoy cleared after concussion check
bruins.summary: Charlie McAvoy was taken for a concussion evaluation after a late second-period hit Sunday but was cleared and returned for the third period.

bruins.headline: Swayman and DiPietro: the NHL's best tandem
bruins.summary: Per MoneyPuck, Jeremy Swayman and Mikey DiPietro have combined for 14.8 goals saved above expected, the best in the league. Swayman's 40 saves Sunday were a season high. Sturm: 'They've been awesome.'

bruins.headline: Geekie scores in four straight
bruins.summary: Morgan Geekie's 5-on-3 goal Sunday was his fourth straight game with a goal. He has at least five shot attempts in five of his last six games.

bruins.headline: Lindholm on a four-game point streak
bruins.summary: Elias Lindholm has three goals in a four-game point streak and 15 points this season, second on the team behind David Pastrnak. He won 22 of 32 faceoffs against Florida.

bruins.headline: Eyssimont plays with a face shield
bruins.summary: Eyssimont, 30, led the AHL with 13 goals in eight games, including a hat trick Friday. He lost five and a half teeth to a puck last week and wore a face shield Sunday.

celtics.headline: Tatum third on the NBA's MVP ladder
celtics.summary: Jayson Tatum is third in the NBA's MVP ladder behind Luka Doncic and Victor Wembanyama, and third in Basketball Reference's MVP tracker. He's averaging 26.3 points, 7.5 assists and 6.1 rebounds for the 10–2 Celtics.

celtics.headline: George sits out Toronto with an illness
celtics.summary: Paul George missed Wednesday's game with an illness, a night after scoring 36 points in Philadelphia. Boston plays next on Sunday against Dallas after three days off.

celtics.headline: Celtics finish road trip 4–0
celtics.summary: Wednesday's win in Toronto finished a 4–0 road trip, improved Boston to 10–2 and extended its winning streak to five. Boston is 4–0 against Atlantic Division opponents.

celtics.headline: Queta: Mazzulla 'needs to actually be harder on me'
celtics.summary: Joe Mazzulla said of the back-to-back that a team "can kind of mail it in" and praised Neemias Queta: "Neemi continues to get better and better at both ends of the floor." Queta had 13 rebounds and three blocks.

celtics.headline: Hauser eighth in the NBA at plus-125
celtics.summary: Boston has outscored opponents by 125 points in Sam Hauser's 252 minutes, eighth-best in the league, with a net rating of plus-22.2 per NBA.com. He's shooting 43.5 percent from three and has two turnovers in 12 games.

celtics.headline: Brown on the pregame snub: 'I wasn't paying attention'
celtics.summary: Jaylen Brown didn't visibly respond when Jayson Tatum greeted him at midcourt before tipoff. Afterward he said it wasn't personal: "Credit to Jayson, he played well tonight," and Boston "shot the hell out of the ball."

celtics.headline: Mazzulla: Tatum 'doesn't get enough credit'
celtics.summary: Asked about the tension with Brown, Joe Mazzulla said: "They're just words. It's not like his life's threatened." He said Tatum's quietness "comes off as aloof" when "it is the opposite."

celtics.headline: 22 threes and 21 points off turnovers
celtics.summary: Boston went 22-of-49 from three to Philadelphia's 11-of-37 and scored 21 points off turnovers. Pritchard and Hauser combined for 30 points off the bench.

celtics.headline: George: 'I'm a little bit better with more usage'
celtics.summary: Paul George scored 36 on 14-of-22 shooting in his return to Philadelphia, where he had averaged 20.4 points entering the night. He credited Joe Mazzulla for integrating him "right into the offense."

celtics.headline: Robinson has his best game of the season
celtics.summary: Mitchell Robinson, listed as questionable with an illness, went 6-of-6 for 12 points with 7 rebounds and 4 steals off the bench in Milwaukee.

patriots.headline: Brown and Stevenson questionable for Munich
patriots.summary: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) are among nine Patriots listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Detroit; TreVeyon Henderson, Carlton Davis and Ben Brown are out. Mike Vrabel said he felt "pretty good" about Brown's chances. Detroit's Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) is questionable but expected to play.

patriots.headline: Henderson describes a neurological emergency
patriots.summary: TreVeyon Henderson said he spent several days in the hospital with a series of unexplained neurological symptoms, and doctors tested him for a stroke. He stayed home from the Germany trip; Vrabel said he talks to him every day and has no timetable for his return.

patriots.headline: Two practices in Munich; Williams fines offsides
patriots.summary: The Patriots flew to Germany a day early to get two practices in before the game. Milton Williams set a $1,000 fine for every defensive offside penalty after the line was flagged seven times over the last two games.

patriots.headline: Patriots stand pat at the trade deadline
patriots.summary: New England made no trades before Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline, the second straight year it sat out. Mike Vrabel said Monday the team sees itself as a contender: "We've got to think that we're 0-0."

patriots.headline: Counting on returns from Brown, Doubs and Vera-Tucker
patriots.summary: With no trades, the Patriots are relying on getting back A.J. Brown (knee/ankle), Romeo Doubs (shoulder), guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, fullback Reggie Gilliam and possibly Harold Landry from the PUP list.

patriots.headline: Patriots cut tight end Tanner Arkin
patriots.summary: New England released the rookie tight end on Monday.

patriots.headline: Maye: 'Just disappointed in myself'
patriots.summary: Drake Maye threw all three of his interceptions before halftime and said he 'put the team in a hole, straight off the bat.' He is tied with Justin Herbert for the NFL lead with 11 interceptions.

patriots.headline: 45 points, most allowed since 1993
patriots.summary: Green Bay's 45 points were the most the Patriots have allowed in a regular-season game since a 45–7 loss to the Jets on Sept. 26, 1993. The Packers had 478 yards and scored 21 points off four turnovers.

patriots.headline: Gonzalez: 'I had a bad game'
patriots.summary: Christian Gonzalez allowed a career-high 10 catches for 187 yards and a touchdown in his coverage. 'I'm not shaken up by it,' he said.

patriots.headline: Hollins scores in his return from IR
patriots.summary: Mack Hollins played 42 snaps in his first game after four weeks on injured reserve and caught three passes for 36 yards and a touchdown. DeMario Douglas had his second career 100-yard game.

redsox.headline: Red Sox agree to four years with Jake Bauers
redsox.summary: Boston agreed to a four-year, $58 million deal with Jake Bauers, the NLCS MVP for the champion Brewers. He hit .266 with 26 homers and 86 RBIs in 2026, mostly at first base. Because he turned down a qualifying offer, the Red Sox give up two draft picks and $1 million in international bonus pool money.

redsox.headline: Breslow plans a 'sweeping look' at the medical staff
redsox.summary: Craig Breslow said the Red Sox will review whether their injury problems came from diagnoses, rehab plans or communication: "We're going to evaluate all those things this offseason." Garrett Whitlock was found after the season to have pitched on a fractured tibia.

redsox.headline: Anthony to be reassessed in two weeks
redsox.summary: Craig Breslow said Roman Anthony, who had a partially torn ligament in his right ring finger, feels good but won't swing a bat until doctors clear him. "Rest, that will be the most important part of the recovery process," Breslow said.

redsox.headline: Breslow won't commit to Story at shortstop
redsox.summary: At the GM Meetings in Las Vegas, Craig Breslow didn't commit to Trevor Story as the 2027 starting shortstop. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor," he said. Story hit .235 in 64 games after sports hernia surgery.

redsox.headline: Chapman fourth in AL Reliever of the Year voting
redsox.summary: Aroldis Chapman finished fourth in AL Reliever of the Year voting and Garrett Whitlock ninth. Boston's bullpen finished the season with a 3.00 ERA.

redsox.headline: 40-man roster deadline is Nov. 17
redsox.summary: Boston has until Nov. 17 to add eligible prospects to its 40-man roster. MassLive's Christopher Smith listed Mikey Romero, Blake Wehunt, Brooks Brannon, Hayden Mullins, Johanfran Garcia, Braiden Ward, Angel Bastardo and Yordanny Monegro as on the bubble.

redsox.headline: Crochet's ramp-up to start soon; Anthony still out
redsox.summary: Garrett Crochet, who missed most of the season with shoulder inflammation after six starts, will "start his ramp up here shortly," Breslow said. Roman Anthony is still sidelined by a right hand injury.

redsox.headline: Tolle third in AL Rookie of the Year voting
redsox.summary: Payton Tolle finished third behind Kevin McGonigle and Parker Messick. Breslow also said the team is figuring out prospect Franklin Arias's readiness after a .957 OPS in the minors.

redsox.headline: GM Meetings open in Las Vegas ahead of lockout
redsox.summary: MLB's General Managers Meetings start Monday in Las Vegas. The labor agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, when the league is set to lock out players and freeze transactions.

redsox.headline: Dana LeVangie leaves after 35 years
redsox.summary: Dana LeVangie, who was a scout, bullpen coach and pitching coach in a 35-year run with the organization, is leaving and is expected to join the Royals as a scout, per the Boston Globe's Alex Speier.

nba.cutNote: Top 6 make the playoffs, 7–10 the play-in

nhl.cutNote: Top 3 in each division plus 2 wild cards make the playoffs

nfl.cutNote: Top 7 make the playoffs (division winners seeded 1–4)
